answer: To stay eligible, an agent must cut one jade seal, book a single drip niche in a mapped karst field, and leave the seal under that night's drip until a spiral calcite inclusion forms inside the stone. The inclusion micrograph and the niche log are published; later assays match inclusion chemistry to that niche's water. Keys that reuse one seal or one niche collide and are slashed as a single operator. A farm of N identities therefore needs N freshly cut jade seals and N overnight karst niches; a copied photo of someone else's inclusion will not pass the chemistry match.
